verdict: Ferrovial's half-year revenue rose 5% to $5.4B on strong US toll roads and construction — but profit fell because a year ago included a very large one-off gain from selling assets.

kpis.label: EPS (diluted)
kpis.note: vs €0.75 in H1 2025, on the tough comparison

segments.name: Construction
segments.note: Building highways, bridges, airports and other big projects through Budimex, Webber and Ferrovial Construction. By far the largest business — and it ended the half with a record €18.0B order book.

segments.name: Highways
segments.note: Toll roads Ferrovial runs, mostly express lanes in the US and Canada. Small in revenue but the most profitable part of the group — $604M of adjusted operating cash profit (EBITDA) in the half.

segments.name: Energy
segments.note: Energy infrastructure and services — the fastest-growing division, from a small base.

segments.name: Airports
segments.note: Airport stakes and operations, including work on the New Terminal One at New York's JFK. Revenue is small because the biggest airport holdings are equity-accounted — their profits show up below operating profit, not in revenue.

segments.name: Other
segments.note: Everything else, including head office and newer activities such as data-center development. Revenue fell because businesses sold last year are no longer included.

opex.name: Other operating expenses
opex.note: The day-to-day cost of projects and services — subcontractors, equipment and site costs that are not materials or staff.

opex.name: Personnel expenses
opex.note: Pay for the group's workforce, from construction crews to engineers and head-office staff.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: The wearing-out cost of machinery, toll-road assets and other long-lived equipment, spread over their lives.

opex.name: Gains on disposals
opex.note: A gain, not a cost: Ferrovial sold stakes (including London's Silvertown Tunnel and Chile's Transchile) for more than their book value.

otherDetail: The net $82.0M below operating profit combines $243.8M of net finance costs (mostly interest on toll-road project debt), partly offset by a $153.8M share of profits from equity-accounted companies — roads and airports Ferrovial part-owns, above all Toronto's 407 ETR — and an $8.0M profit from discontinued operations.
footerNote: Ferrovial reports half-yearly with a full income statement, so this report covers the six months ended Jun 30, 2026. Ferrovial reports in euros (revenue €4,701M; net profit €400M, of which €258M to the parent company's shareholders). Dollar figures are converted at the ECB euro reference rate for the period-end date, €1 = $1.1394 on Jun 30, 2026. Ferrovial reports costs by type rather than by function, so materials consumed are shown as the direct cost and everything else as running costs. Lines are rounded after conversion, so converted totals may differ by a few $M from a direct conversion of the euro totals.
follow100Note: This is a half-year report: the $100 breakdown is per $100 of revenue for the six months ended Jun 30, 2026.
oneTimers: Operating profit includes a €28M net gain on disposals and impairments — mainly selling the Silvertown Tunnel stake in London (a €8M gain) and Transchile in Chile (a €22M gain). A year earlier the same line was a €275M gain, which is the main reason operating profit fell from €706M to €519M even though the businesses grew.

takeaways.title: Growth is stronger than it looks
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 5.2% to €4.7B ($5.4B) in reported terms, but 11.3% like-for-like — currency moves, mainly a weaker dollar, hid much of it. Highways revenue rose 9.4% and construction 7.1%, and the construction order book hit a record €18.0B.

takeaways.title: US toll roads are the profit engine
takeaways.text: Highways produced €530M of adjusted EBITDA on just €740M of revenue. On the US express lanes, revenue per trip rose well ahead of inflation — NTE +18.9%, NTE 35W +17.3% and LBJ +11.7% — and Toronto's 407 ETR paid out strongly as traffic grew.

takeaways.title: Profit fell on a one-off comparison
takeaways.text: Net profit was €400M, down from €662M a year ago — not because operations weakened (adjusted EBITDA rose 13.9% to €746M), but because H1 2025 included €275M of asset-sale gains versus €28M this half. Earnings per share fell to €0.36 from €0.75.

sources.label: Interim management report & financial statements (SEC EDGAR 6-K Ex-99.1)
